chapters.intro: Everything you need to pay, ask a price, and buy the right amount in a Dutch shop or market. Tap 🔊 to hear each phrase in a natural voice.

sections.title: Euros, cents & the comma
sections.body: The currency is the euro (€) and 1 euro = 100 cent. Dutch writes prices with a comma for the decimal, so € 3,50 is said 'drie euro vijftig'. A dot marks thousands, so € 1.250 is one thousand two hundred fifty euro. You almost never say the word 'cent' out loud: € 2,99 is simply 'twee euro negenennegentig'.

sections.title: Vragen naar de prijs
sections.note: Use these at any counter, market stall or shop.

items.en: How much is it all together?

items.nl: Dat is bij elkaar tien euro.
items.en: That comes to ten euros in total.

items.nl: Mag het een onsje meer zijn?
items.en: May it be a little more? (common at the deli)
Do you perhaps have the exact amount?

sections.title: Betalen: pinnen of contant
sections.note: Most shops prefer the pin (debit card); some are pin-only.

sections.title: Bon, korting & prijs
sections.note: Useful words around the till and the price tag.

sections.title: Hoeveelheden in de winkel
sections.note: A pond is 500 g and an ons is 100 g — handy at the market and the cheese counter.

items.en: a bunch (e.g. of flowers or radishes)

sections.title: Maten: kleding & schoenen
sections.note: Use 'maat' for a clothing or shoe size; the number follows.

items.nl: Heeft u dit een maat groter?
items.en: Do you have this one size bigger?

sections.title: Reading a price tag
sections.body: On a label you often see 'per stuk' (each), 'per kilo', '2 voor € 3' (2 for 3 euro) and 'van € 5 voor € 3' (was 5, now 3). 'op = op' means once it is gone, it is gone. A small unit price under the big price helps you compare offers.

sections.q: U koopt kaas. De verkoper vraagt: 'Hoeveel mag het zijn?' Wat antwoordt u als u 300 gram wilt?
sections.qEn: You are buying cheese. The seller asks how much you want. What do you say for 300 grams?
sections.explanation: Cheese and cold cuts are ordered in ons (100 g each), so 300 g is 'drie ons'. A kilo would be far too much and a liter is for liquids.

chapters.intro: How to open, build and close a Dutch letter, email or message — and when to be formal or informal. Tap 🔊 to hear each phrase in a natural voice.

sections.title: Formal or informal?
sections.body: Choose your tone by who reads it. Formal (to a company, the gemeente, a landlord, a doctor) uses 'u' and a polite opening and closing. Informal (to a friend or family) uses 'je/jij' and a relaxed greeting. When in doubt for an official letter, stay formal.

sections.title: Openingen (begin)
sections.note: Pick one line to start. 'Geachte' is the most formal; 'Hoi' is the most casual.

items.en: Dear Sir or Madam, (formal, name unknown)
Dear Ms De Vries, (formal, name known)

sections.title: De inhoud (waarom u schrijft)
sections.note: Open the body with the reason, then your request. Use 'u' forms in a formal letter.

items.en: I am writing to you because...
Would you be able to...? (more polite)
Please find enclosed... / Herewith I send...
Thank you in advance for your reply.

sections.title: Afsluitingen (einde)
sections.note: Match the closing to the opening: formal with formal, casual with casual.

sections.title: Mini-templates
sections.body: Request: Geachte heer/mevrouw, + Ik schrijf u omdat ik ... wil. Zou u ... kunnen? + Alvast bedankt. + Met vriendelijke groet. Complaint: Geachte heer/mevrouw, + Ik ben niet tevreden over ... omdat ... Ik wil graag een oplossing. + Met vriendelijke groet. Cancellation: Geachte heer/mevrouw, + Hierbij zeg ik mijn abonnement op per [datum]. Kunt u dit bevestigen? + Met vriendelijke groet.

sections.title: Handige zinnen voor klacht & opzeggen
sections.note: Building blocks for a complaint or to cancel something.

items.nl: Hierbij zeg ik mijn abonnement op.

items.en: I want to end my contract.
I look forward to hearing from you.

sections.title: Layout tip
sections.body: In a formal letter, put the date and place at the top (Amsterdam, 4 juni 2026), then a short subject line ('Betreft: opzegging abonnement'), then your opening. Keep paragraphs short and end with the closing on its own line, your name underneath.

sections.q: Schrijf een korte formele e-mail aan uw verhuurder. De verwarming is kapot en u wilt dat hij die snel maakt.
sections.qEn: Write a short formal email to your landlord. The heating is broken and you want it fixed quickly.
sections.answer: Geachte heer Bakker, Ik schrijf u omdat de verwarming in mijn woning kapot is. Het is sinds maandag koud in huis en de verwarming wordt niet warm. Zou u dit zo snel mogelijk kunnen laten maken? Ik hoor graag wanneer de monteur kan komen. Alvast bedankt voor uw reactie. Met vriendelijke groet, Ayhan Cerci
sections.explanation: It opens formally with 'Geachte heer', states the reason ('Ik schrijf u omdat...'), makes a polite request with 'Zou u ... kunnen?', asks for a reply, and closes with 'Met vriendelijke groet' and a name — all in 'u' form.
